technique.how: Ask packs per day and years smoked; pack-years = packs/day x years (20 cigarettes = 1 pack). Record current vs former status and quit date. Thresholds studied: >40 pack-years (CARE-COAD1) and >=70 pack-years (Badgett).
technique.prerequisites: Reliable history from patient or informant.

interpretation.positive_finding: >40 pack-years strongly favours obstructive airway disease (LR 8.3) in patients with known, suspected, or no OAD; with prior COPD diagnosis, >=70 pack-years plus prior diagnosis had specificity 100%.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of heavy smoking does not exclude airflow limitation; the LR for absence was not reported in the abstract.
interpretation.pitfalls: Pack-year recall is imprecise; the finding predicts chronic OAD, not whether today's dyspnea is a COPD exacerbation versus pneumonia, ACS, or PE. Heavy smoking also raises probability of ACS, lung cancer and ILD.
interpretation.changes_what: Heavy pack-year history should raise COPD/ILD on the dyspnea differential and prompt spirometry once stable; it does not discriminate the acute cause.

estimates.target_condition: Obstructive airway disease (FEV1 and FEV1/FVC below 5th percentile) - finding: smoking >40 pack-years
estimates.population: 309 consecutive adults at 25 primary care and referral sites in 14 countries; 25% known OAD, 37% suspected, 39% neither
estimates.reference_standard: Spirometry: FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio < 5th percentile adjusted for height, age, sex
estimates.quote: smoking for more than 40 pack-years (LR, 8.3), self-reported history of chronic OAD (LR, 7.3)

sources.citation: Straus SE, McAlister FA, Sackett DL, Deeks JJ. The accuracy of patient history, wheezing, and laryngeal measurements in diagnosing obstructive airway disease. CARE-COAD1 Group. JAMA. 2000;283(14):1853-1857.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use pack-years to attribute acute dyspnea to COPD when PE, ACS, pneumothorax, or heart failure are plausible.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Heavy smokers with acute chest pain or dyspnea need ACS and PE considered independently of COPD history.

extraction_notes: Straus 2000 abstract reports LR 8.3 for >40 pack-years without a CI (multivariate model); full text not in PMC so CI and sens/spec could not be seen; CI left null. Badgett 1993 sens 40%/spec 100% is for the two-variable historical model (prior COPD diagnosis and >=70 pack-years), entered as COMPOSITE; specificity 100% makes LR+ undefined so LR fields are null. Holleman & Simel 1995 RCE listed as anchor but its PubMed record has no abstract and the full text is not open access, so no numbers were taken from it. Straus: 'Patients having all 4 findings had an LR of 220 (ruling in OAD); those with none had an LR of 0.13' (Abstract, Results) - composite, not entered.
